payload.rationale: Historically, measles cases in the United States have rarely exceeded 1,000 since the disease was declared eliminated in 2000. The highest recent peak was 1,274 cases in 2019. Reaching over 6,000 cases in a single year would require a massive, unprecedented outbreak or a catastrophic collapse in vaccination coverage, which is highly unlikely to occur. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that the US maintains strong public health infrastructure and high overall MMR vaccination rates, which typically contain outbreaks quickly, making even a few hundred cases uncommon. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is if there has been a severe, undetected drop in vaccination rates in multiple large communities, combined with simultaneous introductions of the virus, leading to an exponential spread that overwhelms local health departments.
limitations: No current data or CDC reports for 2026 are provided, requiring reliance on historical base rates.
Lack of information on recent trends in vaccine hesitancy or localized outbreaks leading up to September 2026.
